input: Under this inventory policy for a spare motor, the safety stock is set at 1856 units, which gives a reorder point of 20916 units. Demand for the motor averages 3812 units per week, with a standard deviation of 1006 units per week, and replenishment takes 5 weeks. At a 95% cycle service level, the stock that is held against demand variation over the lead time is 1856 units; the reorder point is calculated by adding that cover to the demand that is expected during the 5 weeks of lead time, at 3812 units per week, so that an order placed at the reorder point will arrive, on average, just as the cover begins to be used. The cycle service level can be understood as the probability that a replenishment cycle ends without a stockout occurring, and the safety stock is essentially what converts that probability into units on the shelf. It is important to note that the policy treats demand as normal and independent between weeks, and seasonal peaks are excluded from the calculation. This means that a seasonal peak is effectively outside the protection that the policy provides: demand above the average in a peak week will draw on the safety stock faster than the policy assumes, and the 95% service level holds only for the demand pattern that the policy describes.
